title: Tax-Loss Selling Pressure
market_behavior: Losing securities may experience seasonal selling pressure from investors realizing tax losses, followed by rebound or normalization.
forced_actor: Taxable investors, advisors harvesting losses, and funds managing year-end tax exposure.
why_edge_might_exist: Tax-motivated selling is not purely return-seeking and may create temporary pressure in securities with large prior losses.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: Effects may be small, crowded, calendar-dependent, sensitive to tax regimes, and more available in less-liquid securities with limited capacity.
capacity_hypothesis: Likely lower in small-cap or less-liquid names; personal-capital capacity may exist where spreads do not consume the rebound.
observable_predictions: Large year-to-date losers show abnormal late-year pressure and early-year rebound after controls.
The effect is stronger where taxable ownership and liquidity pressure are plausible.
falsification_tests: Reject if the rebound disappears after spread and liquidity assumptions.
Reject if results depend on survivorship-biased universes.
Weaken if the effect is absent across multiple tax years or only works after threshold tuning.
references: Academic literature on tax-loss selling and January effects
Practitioner research on tax-loss harvesting calendars
